ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C., 1985, c. C-44, as amended, ss. 21.1-21.4 (register of individuals with significant control), s. 263.1 (offences); Canada Business Corporations Regulations, 2001, SOR/2001-512, ss. 12-13; Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17, as amended, ss. 9(2)-9(6), s. 69.1 (record keeping, identity verification and beneficial ownership requirements for reporting entities); Criminal Code, R.S.C., 1985, c. C-46, s. 83.05 (terrorist property listing); Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 17, and related regulations; United Nations Act, S.C. 2001, c. 12; Controlled Goods Act, S.C. 2001, c. 20, and Controlled Goods Regulations, SOR/2019-298; Public Services and Procurement Canada: Canadian Industrial Security Program and Controlled Goods Directive. Current status: CBCA ISC registers are internal to the corporation and are not searchable by the general public; FINTRAC, law enforcement and prescribed authorities may compel access; the Government of Canada has announced a phased transition toward a publicly accessible beneficial ownership registry, but until operational, UBO disclosure is government-only access.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Compliance of each foreign corporate shareholder or parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of companies or equivalent competent authority in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where the country of origin is a party to the 1961 Hague Convention; otherwise Consular Legalization through the Canadian embassy or consulate in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency / Register of Directors and Officers for each foreign corporate shareholder or parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary, director or authorized agent of the foreign entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization followed by Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization, as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copies of passport/state-issued national identity card for every proposed director, officer and individual with significant control (UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority or notary public qualified to certify copies
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized certified copies followed by Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization if the certification is a public/official act in the document origin state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn UBO declaration and source of wealth/funds statement
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Each ultimate beneficial owner, sworn before a notary public or commissioner for oaths
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization and, where required by the legalization authority, Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney irrevocably or revocably appointing the Canadian incorporation agent / registered office agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign corporate board or individual grantor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized board resolution or individual declaration, then Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization, depending on the origin jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source of capital confirmation for the initial capitalization and expected government/diplomatic payment rails
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank of the transferor or foreign parent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Authenticated banker's certificate, notarization, and Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization if the letter is relied on as an sworn instrument

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers, shareholders, UBOs, counterparties and intermediaries against (i) Global Affairs Canada's consolidated Canadian autonomous sanctions list issued under the Special Economic Measures Act and related regulations; (ii) the Criminal Code Part II.1 terrorist listings; (iii) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; (iv) the U.S. OFAC SDN and non-SDN sectoral sanctions lists for US nexus and USD clearing; and (v) relevant provincial securities and enforcement orders. Because the target activity is the manufacture of armored security personnel transport vehicles, each entity and every UBO must undergo enhanced due diligence consistent with FINTRAC guidance on politically exposed persons (PEP), including identification of source of funds and source of wealth, independent corroboration of corporate and military procurement relationships, and enhanced ongoing monitoring. The applicant must execute a sanctions/PEP negative certification and consent to FinTRAC reporting. Any cracked or vague nominal shareholders without disclosed underlying persons will not be accepted.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Corporations Canada - ISED Online Filing Centre and NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automatic Name Search) real-time name search portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Federal corporate names may be in English, French, or both; a name in an official language must be distinctive and avoid confusion with existing names or registered trademarks as assessed by the NUANS search. If the proposed name contains a non-official language element, a transliteration into roman script and a translation must be supplied; the legal element must be in an acceptable Canadian corporate form (e.g., Inc., Corp., Incorporated, Corporation, Canada; or the French equivalents). The name must include a distinctive element and a descriptive element, and may not consist solely of a generic word. In the context of defense manufacturing, the Director will reject names that falsely imply government sponsorship, Crown authorization, military command authority, or certification by national defense institutions.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, banker, banking - prior approval under the Bank Act and/ or OSFI authorization required
Trust, trust company, loan, loan company, finance, lending - regulated financial services licensing required
Insurance, assurance, insurance company - prior insurer licensing required

Royal, Crown, Government of Canada, Privy Council, Federal, Dominion, State, Police, Army, Navy, Air Force, Royal Canadian Mounted Police, NATO - implication of Crown/government/military authority prohibited unless expressly authorized
University, College, Institute, Academy - prior authorization from competent education authorities required if meant as educational institution
Co-operative, cooperative, caisse, credit union - regulated business name requiring applicable provincial or federal incorporation consent
Canada / Canadian - federal approval restrictions apply where the name suggests direct incorporation by the Crown or a Canadian government department

Defence, Defense, Military, Armored, Arsenal, Munitions - accepted only where business licensing documents clearly evidence compliance with export control and controlled goods regimes and the name does not imply state-endorsed contractor status
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a name rejection, Corporations Canada issues a written refusal or request for amendment with the legal basis under sections 12 and 13 of the Canada Business Corporations Act. The applicant may, before the expiry of the 90-day reservation, (i) request a name reservation extension if the underlying NUANS search remains materially identical; (ii) file written submissions to the Director explaining why the proposed name is not confusing, or attach the written consent of the prior name/trademark owner; (iii) file a revised name formula for a new NUANS search; and (iv) if the Director maintains the refusal, apply to the Federal Court for judicial review under section 18.1 of the Federal Courts Act, R.S.C., 1985, c. F-7. In parallel, the incorporation counsel should reserve a fallback acceptable name so that the federal incorporation filing is not delayed beyond the 90-day window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as the sole registered office for a federal corporation. The Canada Business Corporations Act, section 19, requires the registered office to be situated at a place in Canada and to be a physical address where process may be served. A virtual mail-forwarding address or postal box cannot satisfy service-of-process requirements. A licensed registered-agent office with a physical street address and on-site acceptance of legal process may be used for the registered office, but for armored vehicle manufacturing under ISIC 3040, the regulator will expect an operational facility, security-controlled premises, and verifiable commercial substance in Canada before issuing controlled goods registration, defense authorization, or government tender eligibility.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High - quantified risk of approximately 75-85% for unannounced physical inspections over the first 24 months. Trigger authorities include the Controlled Goods Directorate under the Controlled Goods Act, the Canadian Industrial Security Program for classified or export-controlled content, Public Services and Procurement Canada industrial security officers, provincial occupational health and safety authorities for manufacturing workplaces, and FINTRAC-/DFAIT-led trade-control compliance checks. The applicant should expect on-site verification of UBO records, board/office books, security clearance documents, arms/controlled goods movement logs, and segregation between the Canadian defence line and foreign military sales.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, including sections 6-12 (articles and incorporation), section 21 (corporate records), sections 102-115 (directors and governance), and sections 121-126 (officers and conflict rules).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation under the Canada Business Corporations Act, generally filed using Corporations Canada Form 1, together with the registered-office and first-director information required by the Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies. Shares may be issued without par value for consideration determined by the directors, subject to the Canada Business Corporations Act. Canadian federal law does not require a capital escrow account for incorporation. The corporation must maintain proper stated-capital, share-issuance, securities-register, and accounting records.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT the Corporation accept and record the subscriptions for the shares specified in the incorporation documents upon receipt of the agreed consideration; that its registered office be established at the address stated in the Articles or subsequently filed notice; that [Name] be appointed President, [Name] Secretary, and [Name] Treasurer, each to serve until replaced or removed; that the officers are authorized to obtain banking, tax, insurance, and licensing arrangements; and that the officers are authorized to execute all documents and filings necessary to give effect to these resolutions, subject to the Canada Business Corporations Act and applicable federal, provincial, municipal, export-control, controlled-goods, occupational-health, environmental, and defence-procurement requirements.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm Federal Eligibility and Corporate Name
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada online filing service or Corporations Canada contact centre.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Select a word name or request a numbered corporation. Conduct a Nuans corporate-name search where a word name is proposed. Confirm the registered office is physically located in Canada and identify the first directors, share classes, restrictions, and transfer provisions.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name or numbered-company request
Nuans name search report, if applicable
Restrictions on share transfers and business restrictions, if applicable
Beneficial ownership and control information for compliance records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to a name or completeness query through Corporations Canada, amend the proposed name or articles, and resubmit the corrected filing with any additional fee requested.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and File Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada online filing service, or Corporations Canada paper filing channel.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form 1 or the online equivalent, identify the registered office and first directors, attach any required schedules, certify the information, and pay the applicable filing fee. Signatures may be electronic where accepted by the filing channel; documents requiring notarization should be notarized before submission by an authorized Canadian notary or commissioner.
required_dossiers: Registered-agent or authorized-filer information, if used
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct rejected fields, replace an unacceptable name, provide missing schedules, and resubmit through the same Corporations Canada channel. Preserve the original filing reference and written query.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada and the corporation's registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Download and retain the Certificate of Incorporation, Articles, and filing confirmation. Establish the minute book, securities register, shareholder register, director register, and register of individuals with significant control. Maintain records at the registered office or another permitted Canadian location and update them after every issuance, transfer, or governance change.
required_dossiers: Register of individuals with significant control
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct corporate records promptly, file any required amendment or notice, and obtain a certificate or corporate-profile correction from Corporations Canada where the registry record is inaccurate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Organizational Governance and Share Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporation's board of directors, with Corporations Canada for filings where required.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Pass the first board resolution, appoint officers, approve banking authority, adopt the registered office, approve the fiscal year, authorize tax registrations, and issue shares only after receiving the approved consideration. Obtain written director consents where permitted and document conflicts of interest. File changes to registered-office, director, or other prescribed information within the applicable statutory period.
required_dossiers: Proof of consideration and share certificates or electronic records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify defective resolutions or issuances by board approval, obtain shareholder approval where legally required, correct the securities register, and file any overdue statutory notice with an explanatory record.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for Tax, Payroll, Import, and Provincial Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency, Canada Border Services Agency, and the applicable provincial corporate registry and tax authorities.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain a Business Number and register applicable GST/HST, payroll, corporate income-tax, import-export, and provincial accounts. Register extra-provincially in each province or territory where the corporation carries on business, maintains premises, employs personnel, or holds inventory. Obtain municipal business, zoning, and occupancy approvals before commencing operations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct registration data, submit missing supporting evidence, request a formal review from the responsible authority, and complete late registrations with required penalty and interest remediation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Controlled-Goods and Defence Trade Compliance Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Controlled Goods Directorate, Public Works and Procurement Canada; Global Affairs Canada Trade Controls Bureau; and, where applicable, the United States Department of State or Department of Commerce.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Determine whether the proposed vehicles, components, technical data, software, or manufacturing activities involve controlled goods, controlled technology, defence articles, or export-controlled items. Register under the Controlled Goods Program before examining, possessing, or transferring controlled goods where required. Appoint a designated official, implement a security plan, screen personnel, control visitors and records, and obtain export permits before controlled exports. Obtain any required security clearance for Canadian defence procurement.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to regulator requests, correct the security plan or registration application, suspend controlled access pending approval, and use the applicable reconsideration, review, or appeal process for a refusal or compliance direction.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No single federal industrial manufacturing licence generally applies. The principal federal authority for controlled defence goods is the Controlled Goods Directorate, Public Works and Procurement Canada. Provincial ministries, municipalities, and local authorities issue facility, zoning, building, fire, occupational-health, environmental, hazardous-material, and emissions approvals.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Controlled Goods Program Registration; supplemented by applicable provincial manufacturing, environmental, building, fire, occupational-health, zoning, hazardous-material, and municipal occupancy approvals.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Impact Assessment Agency of Canada, together with the applicable provincial environmental regulator.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Project-specific screening. A normal armoured-vehicle manufacturing facility is generally subject to provincial environmental permitting and is not automatically a designated federal project under the Impact Assessment Act. A federal impact assessment may apply if the project is a designated project or has federal triggers, including certain land, water, hazardous-substance, or federal-funding circumstances.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Obtain provincial permits or approvals for wastewater, stormwater, air emissions, volatile organic compounds, fuel and chemical storage, hazardous waste, contaminated soil, and waste transport. Comply with permit-specific mass, concentration, monitoring, reporting, and operating limits; applicable federal Canadian Environmental Protection Act requirements; municipal sewer bylaws; spill-reporting duties; and provincial hazardous-waste rules. No universal Canada-wide numerical threshold applies to every facility.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain building permits, occupancy approval, fire-code inspection and certification, emergency-response and hazardous-material approvals, and any local civil-protection clearance. Complete structural, seismic where applicable, lifting-equipment, pressure-equipment, electrical, ventilation, and fire-suppression inspections. Comply with the applicable provincial occupational-health and safety statute, workplace hazardous-products requirements, WHMIS, machine guarding, noise, ergonomics, confined-space, respiratory-protection, and incident-reporting rules. Obtain workers' compensation registration and maintain documented safety training, preventive maintenance, emergency plans, and inspection records.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) via My Business Account (MyBA) portal and GST/HST NETFILE
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities obtain a CRA Business Number (BN) by filing Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number) electronically through Business Registration Online or by mail/telephone; federally incorporated corporations under the Canada Business Corporations Act receive an automatic BN and CRA account profile created through Corporations Canada data exchange; the entity must then activate or register its GST/HST account (RT), payroll (RP), and import/export (RM) program accounts via MyBA or EDI; non-resident corporations without a physical Canadian presence must designate a Canadian agent or representative for CRA service correspondence and record access.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; Canadian-resident corporation taxable on worldwide income; provincial income tax allocation based on permanent establishment; no pass-through classification; territorial scope for non-resident shareholders is Canadian-source dividends and capital gains only where applicable; no tax-exempt zone treatment under federal law
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No U.S.-style check-the-box election under CRA practice; statutory elections available under the Income Tax Act include amalgamation elections (s. 87(6)/(11)), winding-up rollover elections (ss. 88(1)/(2)), partnership fair-value elections (s. 96(8)), foreign affiliate excess-EBT hybrid mismatch elections under s. 91(5.1), and ancillary elections for fiscal year, capital cost allowance (schedule 2), and resource pools; these are filed with prescribed CRA forms and timelines

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD $30,000 in taxable supplies (excluding zero-rated exports) made by the entity and all associates over the preceding four calendar quarters; non-resident persons carrying on a Canadian commercial activity must register irrespective of this small-supplier exemption if they are engaged in a commercial activity in Canada and do not meet the threshold
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, API stamping, or digital stamping for commercial invoices; registrants with annual taxable supplies exceeding CAD $1.5M must file GST/HST returns electronically via GST/HST NETFILE or EDI; CRA has an electronic records mandate and may require registered exporters to retain transactional and export documentation in machine-readable format for audit; mandatory CERS (Canadian Export Reporting System) electronic export declarations are required for controlled or regulated exports

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated export supply under Part V of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act when goods are exported by the supplier, or supplied to a non-resident for direct export, and the supplier has documentary proof of export including proof that title and possession passed outside Canada; for all-terrain military tactical vehicles, the exporter must hold a valid export permit and comply with the Export Control List under the Export and Import Permits Act if the goods are controlled, and zero-rating is available for qualifying services provided to non-residents if performed entirely outside Canada or in relation to tangible property situated outside Canada at the time of supply
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Customs Export Declaration (B13A) or CERS electronic export declaration with validated K84 export registration number
Bill of Lading (ocean, air, rail, or truck) showing the consignee, destination, and export date of the military vehicle
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank wire record evidencing that export sales proceeds were credited to a Canadian bank account within the prescribed repatriation period
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess GST/HST and net tax deficiencies within 4 years; the limitation period is waived entirely where misrepresentation, gross negligence, or fraud is established; false or unsupported export zero-rating claims attract civil penalties up to 25% of the net tax deficiency under s. 280 of the Excise Tax Act, arrears interest under s. 280.1, and potential criminal prosecution under s. 327 for knowing misrepresentation; CRA will claw back input tax credits and assessed refunds if the exporter cannot produce the mandatory customs and foreign-exchange documentation within the 180-day repatriation window

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); ultimate FX policy authority rests with the Minister of Finance via the Exchange Fund Account; FINTRAC administers cross-border funds-transfer reporting under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA); OSFI supervises banking soundness and capital adequacy.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a free-floating exchange-rate regime. The CAD is fully convertible on both current and capital accounts; Canada has been in continuous compliance with IMF Article VIII since 1952, prohibiting exchange restrictions on current payments and discriminatory currency practices. No exchange-control permits, surrender requirements, or prior central-bank approvals attach to trade settlement, dividends, interest, royalties, or capital flows. Overlay restrictions are sectoral, not monetary: (i) Investment Canada Act mandatory national-security/net-benefit review for non-Canadian capital into defense-related businesses; (ii) CBCA director-residency rules requiring 25% resident-Canadian directors and at least one resident Canadian on boards of fewer than four; (iii) Controlled Goods Regulations requiring registration with the Controlled Goods Directorate for possession/examination of controlled military goods; (iv) EIPA export-permit coverage from Global Affairs Canada for outward movements of military hardware. Profit repatriation: dividends and interest paid to non-residents attract Part XIII withholding tax (25% statutory, treaty-reduced, e.g., 5%–15% under the Canada-US Treaty); branch remittances attract a 25% Part I.14 branch tax (treaty-reduced). These are fiscal burdens, not convertibility impediments; foreign-currency deposit accounts are freely available at Schedule I banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no statutory repatriation deadline, mandatory conversion ratio, or surrender obligation for export receipts. Exporters may retain foreign currency indefinitely in CAD or foreign-currency accounts at authorized Canadian banks. Ancillary compliance obligations include: (i) FINTRAC electronic funds-transfer reporting for every SWIFT wire of CAD 10,000 or more in a 24-hour period; (ii) export declarations and permit-ledger maintenance under the Customs Act and the Export and Import Permits Act; (iii) Statistics Canada balance-of-payments and CIMT merchandise-trade reporting. For the defense sector, banks independently reconcile inbound export proceeds against the relevant EIPA permit and Controlled Goods Registration; unexplained mismatches or third-country routing trigger Suspicious Transaction Reports. Violations of EIPA or the Defence Production Act create criminal exposure but do not give rise to any currency-surrender obligation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (paid-in capital / escrow hold) and Operational Account (government receivable concentration)
Operational Account and USD foreign-currency clearing account
Operational Account and trade-finance/LC settlement account
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account with US-corridor USD clearing
Operational Account and standby-LC collateral account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: RATING: LOW (0.15–0.20 / 1.00). Canada has no EMI charter class; digital payment firms must register with the Bank of Canada under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA, operative 2024) and with FINTRAC as money services businesses (MSBs). Offshore digital EMIs are functionally non-viable for defense-sector capital flows: Schedule I banks will not route defense receivables through an EMI intermediary due to sanctions and dual-use exposure; EMIs are not Payments Canada members and cannot access Lynx/ACSS; Government Direct Wire settlement requires banking with the Receiver General's designated bank (RBC); and diplomatic LCs require confirmation by a Canadian Schedule I bank. EMIs remain acceptable only for de minimis operational expenses below CAD 10,000 (travel, software, consulting) and must never be used for capital injections, escrow, payroll of controlled-goods personnel, or trade settlements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: PHYSICAL PRESENCE IS MANDATORY for this High_Risk_Special_License sector. At least one director and every individual with signing authority must attend an in-person onboarding interview at the bank's corporate banking centre (Toronto, Ottawa, or Montreal preferred given proximity to DND and PSPC). Fully remote digital onboarding via Verified.Me or equivalent is not available for ISIC 3040 entities. Non-resident directors may be accommodated only with notarized identification, an apostilled police certificate, and an original banker's reference from a qualifying foreign financial institution; video-conference interviews require case-by-case approval by the bank's Financial Intelligence Unit. A physical site visit to the registered office and armored-vehicle assembly facility is standard procedure. Full onboarding cycle is 4–8 weeks from documentation lodgment to active account status.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sectoral red flag — ISIC 3040 / NAICS 336992 military armored vehicle manufacturing; designated high-risk sector with dual-use diversion potential for embargoed states.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Current Controlled Goods Registration Certificate issued by the Controlled Goods Directorate (ISED); (2) complete EIPA export-permit file from Global Affairs Canada covering all target jurisdictions; (3) CGP compliance manual and security-cleared personnel list; (4) deny-party and consolidated-screening procedure; (5) end-user / end-use certificates for all declared military buyers; (6) audited financial statements and purpose-of-account statement; (7) defense product-liability insurance certificate; (8) reference letters from the DND/PSPC procurement office or prior bankers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP and procurement-fraud red flag — invoicing to Government of Canada (DND/PSPC) and foreign diplomatic missions triggers enhanced corruption, kickback, and procurement-integrity scrutiny.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Signed defense procurement contract including RFP and award letter; (2) SRIS (Supplier Registration Information System) registration and positive Integrity Regime attestation against the PSPC debarment list; (3) Secret-level personnel security clearances for key officers; (4) UBO register evidencing absence of domestic or foreign PEP ownership; (5) CRA tax clearance certificate for contract purposes; (6) no-litigation and no-arbitration declaration together with the corporate compliance manual.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership and CBCA residency exposure — foreign controlling shareholders or directors; CGP examination vulnerability for foreign-controlled corporations; opacity of offshore holding layers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Organizational chart from ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) down to the Canadian entity; (2) federal Articles of Incorporation and annual corporate returns; (3) CBCA s.105 declaration of resident-Canadian directors; (4) passports and proof of address for every director; (5) police certificates from all jurisdictions of residence issued within 90 days; (6) original foreign-bank reference letter; (7) source-of-wealth and source-of-funds declarations for non-resident shareholders; (8) CGP-approved mitigation agreement where foreign control exists; (9) CRA business number and historical T2 filings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return under the Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary date of incorporation; due within 60 days after each anniversary month end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fee CAD 100 (approx. USD 74); continued delinquency for two consecutive years may lead to administrative dissolution by Corporations Canada

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual T2 Corporation Income Tax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the corporation's fiscal year end; for non-resident corporations carrying on business in Canada, same six-month rule, with tax installments due monthly or quarterly
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure-to-file penalty is 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month (max 12 months); repeated failure penalty 10% plus 2% per month; criminal prosecution possible for deliberate evasion; CRA may issue demands and freeze bank accounts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fiscal year end plus one month for annual filers; monthly/quarterly filers due one month after reporting period end; instalments due per CRA schedule
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty 5% of net amount owing plus 1% per full month (max 12 months); interest compounded daily at prescribed rate; failure to file electronially when required adds additional penalty

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Registered Charity / Political Contribution Return (if applicable due to defense sector lobbying)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Charity T3010 within six months after fiscal year end; lobbying registry annual return within 30 days of registration end anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Referral to CRA Education and Information Programs; potential revocation of registration or financial penalties under Lobbying Act

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Report under the Canada Not-for-profit Corporations Act (if structured as non-profit) – not applicable for standard CBCA business corporation

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: CBCA requires an independent auditor unless shareholders unanimously waive appointment at each annual meeting; under CBCA, a corporation with gross revenue under CAD 1,000,000 (approx. USD 740,000) at end of fiscal year may apply for exemption from audit if shareholders pass resolution; otherwise independent audit is mandatory irrespective of size. For non-resident extra-provincial registrant, audit requirement generally follows home jurisdiction unless federal license imposes condition.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the Canadian Accounting Standards Board for publicly accountable enterprises; ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) for private companies; Canadian GAAP (Part II, CPA Canada Handbook) acceptable for private federal corporations; CRA taxable income computed under the Income Tax Act using the same accounting framework.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: CBCA does not require an annual UBO filing at the federal level; however, since June 2019, Corporations Canada requires submission of individual name, address, and citizenship of directors with annual return; beneficial ownership information must be recorded in the corporation's register of individuals with significant control (ISC register) and updated in real time, including changes resulting from share transfers. Canada has enacted the Prohibition on the Purchase of Residential Property by Non-Canadians Act but UBO transparency under CBCA is maintained through section 21.1-21.4 registers; failure to maintain ISC register is an offence punishable by fine up to CAD 200,000 (approx. USD 148,000) or imprisonment.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC register)
Minute Book containing resolutions and by-laws

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: CAD 150 – CAD 500 (approx. USD 110 – USD 370) per year for registered office and corporate agent services in a major commercial jurisdiction
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: CAD 3,500 – CAD 12,000 (approx. USD 2,600 – USD 8,900) for a mid-size federal corporation in defense manufacturing; larger defense contractors may exceed CAD 25,000 (approx. USD 18,500)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% small business rate on first $500,000 active business income; 38% general rate on remainder
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SR&ED tax credits (15-20% of qualifying expenditures), manufacturing investment tax credits, accelerated capital cost allowance

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return filed electronically via CRA My Business Account or My Account
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: June 15 following fiscal year-end or six months if later

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate revenue from all sources including exports and government contracts
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents report solely Canadian-source income on Schedule 2; exclude foreign revenue

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after allowable deductions and losses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidation: Non-residents limited to Canadian-source income; no foreign tax credit claimed

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty $50 per day (minimum $100, maximum $5,000); failure to remit tax incurs interest at prescribed rate plus 10% penalty

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% on domestic dividends paid to Canadian residents; 25% statutory rate on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: File Form NR301 with supporting documentation including beneficial ownership certificate; obtain Treaty Relief Certificate (TRC) from CRA prior to payment
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: 0% or 10% under most treaties; Royalties: 5-25% depending on treaty classification and IP type (e.g., 10% standard for patents)

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 50,000,000 gross revenue for Master File requirement; CAD 500,000 related-party transaction threshold for Local File
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: ESR applies exclusively to non-resident entities; Canadian residents subject to GAAR and substance-over-form analysis

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful misrepresentation or omission of income on T2 return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal conviction under Income Tax Act; fines up to $1,000,000 plus 10x tax penalty; imprisonment up to 5 years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability for unpaid taxes; possible director disqualification under Canada Business Corporations Act; travel bans

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Incorporation without real business operations, employees or decision-making in Canada
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR recharacterization; transfer pricing adjustments; penalties up to 10x tax benefit
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil; civil restitution claims; potential criminal charges for fraudulent incorporation

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file CTR or STR with FINTRAC for defense-related payments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to $100,000 per violation; license revocation; criminal prosecution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal fines; imprisonment for willful non-compliance; director disqualification
